response.sql: WITH t AS (SELECT p.player_id, p.death_country, SUM(a.g_1b - a.g_cf) AS total FROM appearances a JOIN player p ON p.player_id = a.player_id WHERE a.g_1b IS NOT NULL AND a.g_cf IS NOT NULL GROUP BY p.player_id, p.death_country), m AS (SELECT AVG(total) AS av FROM t) SELECT SUM(t.total) AS sum_of_totals, AVG(t.total - m.av) AS avg_excess FROM t CROSS JOIN m WHERE t.total > m.av

assumptions.assumption: player_id is unique in player, so each player has one total. Players with a blank (NULL or empty) death country are kept, because the join is on player_id only and does not filter on death_country.

The average total is the unweighted mean of per-player totals. It is taken over every matched player who has at least one row where both g_1b and g_cf are non-null. Players with no such row have no total and are left out of that average.
